name: XML
summary: Learn to read and write well-formed XML documents, escape text, use namespaces, and query a local tree.

prerequisites: Know how to save a plain text file.
A local XML parser such as xmllint or Python ElementTree is useful for the exercises.
metadata.miniProject: Build a small library exchange document. Use one namespaced catalog root and book elements with IDs and titles. Write a local reader that checks for missing IDs and handles escaped text. Keep the format independent of remote resources.

lessons.title: Build a well-formed document tree
lessons.explanation: An XML document has one document element. Opening and closing element names must agree, and nested elements close in the reverse order from which they opened. XML names are case-sensitive. An empty element can use a single self-closing tag.

api.name: document element
api.description: The single root element of the XML document.

lessons.practice: Add a second book with a title. Parse the resulting document locally.
lessons.pitfall: Closing a parent before its child produces a malformed document even if every element name appears twice.

exercise.expected: One catalog root contains two book elements with separate titles.
exercise.completion: Change one closing tag’s case and observe the parse error, then restore it.

lessons.title: Separate attribute values from escaped text
lessons.explanation: Use attributes for short metadata such as an identifier, and elements for structured content. Attribute values use matching quotation marks. A literal ampersand in text is written as & and a literal less-than sign as < when they are meant as data.
lessons.example:
<catalog>
  <book id="b1" category="logic">
    <title>Proof & Practice</title>
    <description>For learners at level < 5.</description>
  </book>
</catalog>

api.name: id="b1"
api.description: Attach a named attribute to the element.

api.name: &
api.description: Represent one literal ampersand in decoded character data.

lessons.practice: Add a book title that includes an ampersand, then inspect the decoded text.
lessons.pitfall: Do not confuse escaped XML source with the text delivered by the parser.

exercise.expected: The parsed title includes an ampersand without the characters amp or a semicolon.
exercise.completion: Compare the raw file with the parsed text and check a value containing a less-than sign.

lessons.title: Use namespace names to keep vocabularies distinct
lessons.explanation: A namespace distinguishes names used by different vocabularies. A prefixed name combines the namespace URI bound to its prefix with the local name. The same URI can be bound to different prefixes. A default namespace applies to unprefixed element names, and does not apply to unprefixed attributes.

api.name: xmlns:study
api.description: Bind the prefix study to a namespace URI in scope.

api.name: study:title
api.description: Name a title element in the vocabulary associated with study.

lessons.practice: Change the prefix study to books in the declarations and element names without changing the URI.
lessons.pitfall: Treat the namespace URI as an identifier. Parsing this document does not require fetching a resource from that URI.

exercise.expected: A namespace-aware parser reports the same expanded names before and after the change.
exercise.completion: Verify that the two title elements remain distinct even though both local names are title.

lessons.title: Find elements relative to a document root
lessons.explanation: A parsed tree exposes elements, attributes, and text separately. In Python ElementTree, root.findall("./book/title") returns matching title children through book children of root. When the document uses a namespace, map its URI to a prefix and use that prefix in the lookup.

api.name: ElementTree.fromstring(text)
api.description: Parse XML text into an element tree root.

api.name: element.findall("./book/title")
api.description: Find titles directly inside the root’s book children.

lessons.practice: Extract only book titles and retain the same output when unrelated notes are added.
lessons.pitfall: Searching for every descendant title would include the notes title. Choose a path that matches the document’s intended shape.

exercise.expected: The result contains Arrays and Loops in document order and excludes Editor notes.
exercise.completion: Add another book and confirm that only its title extends the result.

lessons.title: Validate a small exchange document
lessons.explanation: Well-formed XML can still violate a data contract. An attribute called id has no automatic uniqueness guarantee in this simple document. Validate required elements and uniqueness in the reader or apply a separately defined schema.

api.name: element.get("id")
api.description: In ElementTree, read an attribute or receive a default when it is absent.

api.name: application validation
api.description: Check required fields and business rules after parsing.

lessons.practice: Read the books and report a missing or repeated ID, a blank title, or a nonnumeric duration.
lessons.pitfall: The minutes element contains text until the application converts and validates it as a number.

exercise.expected: A valid catalog produces the ordered list of two book records.
exercise.completion: Check a duplicate ID and a missing duration in separate modified copies.
